//: o9k compatibility registry — the single machine-readable source of truth for which framework claims which concern. detect.mjs, o9k-init.mjs, o9k-guide.mjs, session-start.mjs, o9k-migrate.mjs, host-wire.mjs, skills-sync.mjs and refresh-hosts.mjs all read this file; docs/COMBINING.md is the human-readable rendering of the same facts. Adding a framework = one entry here (+ a matrix row in the docs).

overview.desc: the one repo map / code index per session

memory.note: the o9k-memory hooks prefer TIM; uninstall one to be unambiguous.

memory-integration.desc: hooks wiring a memory backend into sessions

plan.desc: the store that owns work items

roster.desc: role-based model selection + limit-aware dispatch (owned by standalone team-up)

o9k-core.label: o9k-core
o9k-core.audience: Everyone — this is o9k itself: the arbitration table that decides which tool owns which concern, plus the host wiring and /o9k-init, /o9k-guide, /o9k-update, /o9k-stats. Nothing else here works without it.
o9k-core.notFor: Nobody; if you don't want core, you don't want o9k.

o9k-scout.label: o9k-scout
o9k-scout.audience: People working in real codebases, especially large or unfamiliar ones. Stops the 20k-token 'let me look around' burn: search before read, read narrow, one repo map per session.
o9k-scout.notFor: Sessions that touch few files, or work that isn't code at all (writing, research, ops) — there is nothing to be disciplined about.

o9k-dispatch.label: o9k-dispatch
o9k-dispatch.audience: People whose work involves broad sweeps — repo-wide searches, log analysis, digesting long docs, several independent subtasks. Those run in subagents and return conclusions instead of dumping transcripts into your main context.
o9k-dispatch.notFor: Short, single-file, single-thread sessions. Spawning a subagent for a two-file change costs more than it saves.

o9k-memory.label: o9k-memory
o9k-memory.audience: People with projects that span many sessions and who already run (or want) a memory MCP. Gives you a session-start briefing, recall of past decisions, and a state flush before compaction.
o9k-memory.notFor: One-off tasks, throwaway repos, or anyone unwilling to install TIM or hmem — without a backend this pillar has nothing to wire.

o9k-recon.label: o9k-recon
o9k-recon.audience: People who actively curate their tool stack — evaluating new plugins/MCPs, keeping the compatibility matrix current, installing companion bundles. Mostly a maintainer's pillar.
o9k-recon.notFor: Anyone whose stack is settled. Recon is scouting, not day-to-day work; you can install it later the day you go shopping.

superpowers.label: superpowers (methodology plugin)
superpowers.//: 2026-07-17 Benni: dispatch owner = o9k-dispatch; removed dispatch from superpowers concerns (skill dispatching-parallel-agents disabled/archived)

frameworks.//spun-out: Formerly o9k pillars. o9k connects frameworks; it does not ship features of its own. These are now standalone repos that o9k only arbitrates and offers to install.

caveman-mode.label: Caveman Mode (output compression)
caveman-mode.install: claude plugin marketplace add Bumblebiber/caveman-mode && claude plugin install caveman-mode
caveman-mode.audience: Long sessions where the agent's own prose is a real share of the context. Code and safety-critical text stay uncompressed.
caveman-mode.notFor: People who read the agent's output as documentation, or who find telegraphic style harder to follow.

team-up.label: team-up (multi-agent roster + mailbox runs)
team-up.audience: People who drive several CLIs/models at once — planner/implementer/reviewer pipelines, deterministic model picks by role, limit-aware fallback chains.
team-up.notFor: Single-model, single-CLI users. It is a whole orchestration runtime; needs tmux, and on Windows needs WSL.

o9k-statusline.label: o9k-statusline (multi-host status bar)
o9k-statusline.audience: People who want model, context fill, limit headroom, git state and memory project visible at a glance in Claude Code, Cursor or Hermes.
o9k-statusline.notFor: Codex and OpenCode users (no statusline API), and anyone already happy with a custom status bar.

md-provenance.label: md-provenance (markdown attribution)
md-provenance.install: claude plugin marketplace add Bumblebiber/md-provenance && claude plugin install md-provenance
md-provenance.audience: Anyone whose repo fills up with agent-written HANDOFF/PLAN/RESULT files and who later needs to know which agent wrote what, why, and on whose instruction.
md-provenance.notFor: Repos where agents barely write Markdown — the stamps are then pure noise.

bundle-bench.label: bundle-bench (companion stack benchmark)
bundle-bench.install: claude plugin marketplace add Bumblebiber/bundle-bench && claude plugin install bundle-bench
bundle-bench.audience: Maintainers and anyone who wants pass-count and cost numbers for a companion combo instead of trusting READMEs.
bundle-bench.notFor: Casual users — one ablation run costs a normal working session in real tokens.

claudeMem.label: claude-mem
claudeMem.why: hmem is what o9k-memory's hooks are wired to: session-start briefing, deep recall on demand, checkpoint-before-compact, cross-device sync. A second memory writes the same lessons to a place no hook reads — split-brain memory.

mem0.label: mem0
mem0.why: Same memory concern, but hosted and outside the hook wiring — hmem keeps memory local, hook-integrated and inspectable.

graphify.label: Graphify
graphify.why: Index-based overviews bulk-inject retrieved context and go stale between reindexes. Scout builds one canonical map per session from the live tree — no index server, no staleness, and it feeds ast-grep instead of fighting it.

claudeContext.label: claude-context
claudeContext.why: A vector index of the repo is a second overview owner that drifts from the live tree. Scout's per-session map needs no index server and never serves stale results.

codebaseMemory.label: codebase-memory-mcp
codebaseMemory.why: A code knowledge graph is a second overview owner. Scout's one-map-per-session rule delivers the same navigation without the index build and staleness cost.

tokenOptimizer.label: token-optimizer-mcp
tokenOptimizer.why: Same concern, opaque middle-man: it rewrites context in flight. caveman-mode and scout achieve the savings at the source (say less, load less) and stay inspectable — /o9k-stats can prove the effect.

taskMaster.label: task-master
taskMaster.why: Both are plan stores, only one may own work items. beads is a dependency-aware graph with CLI+MCP, plays under the one-plan-owner rule with superpowers, and doesn't claim the methodology spine the way task-master's PRD flow does.

bmad.label: BMAD
bmad.why: One methodology spine, ever. superpowers is the tested one: brainstorm→plan→TDD→review as skills, composes with o9k under a single named arbitration. BMAD also carries its own plan store, colliding with beads too.

specKit.label: spec-kit
specKit.why: One methodology spine, ever. spec-kit wants to own the whole workflow; its specs are project documents that survive in the repo without the tool.

superClaude.label: SuperClaude
superClaude.why: One methodology spine, ever. superpowers composes with o9k under a single named arbitration; SuperClaude's command suite wants the whole workflow.
